reader.title: Shooting of Joseph Wills by a Richmond policeman
bases: A single Richmond police officer shot a Black man he was pursuing to arrest for theft; no crowd or mob took part (A1, A3).
All four reports come from one paper, the Richmond Daily Dispatch, and its account of the shooting rests on the officer's side (A1-A4).

summary.text: The shooting of Joseph Wills was the wounding of a Black man by Richmond, Virginia, police officer Hulcher on November 22, 1880, during an arrest for the alleged theft of a pair of boots.
Wills, who also went by William Jackson, was shot in the left leg, later sentenced to twenty-five lashes for the theft, and then pleaded guilty to resisting the officer.
According to the Richmond Daily Dispatch, at about 5 o'clock on the evening of November 22 a man it called "a negro named Joe Wills" took a pair of boots from a store on Broad Street and ran.
He was pursued and overtaken on Third Street between Franklin and Grace, where Officer Hulcher tried to arrest him.
The paper stated that Wills attacked the officer with "a large pocket-knife" and that Hulcher "was forced" to draw his pistol and fire one shot.
The ball struck Wills in the left leg, causing what the Dispatch called "a painful flesh wound."
He was taken in a wagon to the Second police station, where Dr. Brock dressed the wound.

The next morning Wills appeared before Police-Justice D. C. Richardson, charged with stealing boots from C. W. Green and with resisting and attempting to cut Policeman Hulcher, and his case was continued to December 4.
Tried under the name William Jackson, he was sentenced in Police Court to twenty-five lashes for the theft and sent on to the grand jury on the resisting charge.
On December 9, in the Hustings Court, "Joseph Wills alias William Jackson" pleaded guilty to resisting the officer and was sentenced to thirty days in jail and a $10 fine.
No inquiry into the officer's use of his pistol appears in the coverage, and no report says whether the whipping was carried out.

The only coverage found was in the Daily Dispatch, which reported the shooting in a short local item headed "Shot by a Policeman" and followed the case through its Police Court and Hustings Court columns.
The paper told the story from the officer's side, adding that Wills had served a chain-gang term as William Burwell and was "a noted thief" who "has borne a desperate character."
Its later court notes called him "the colored snatch-thief" and listed his case among routine petty offenses, without comment on the shooting.
No account from Wills or any witness other than the police appears, and no Black newspaper from this period is available to compare.

accounts.label: Police report in the Daily Dispatch
accounts.gist: Wills took boots from a Broad Street store, ran, and when overtaken attacked Officer Hulcher with a large pocket-knife; the officer 'was forced' to fire, hitting him in the leg.

accounts.label: Court record
accounts.gist: Wills was convicted of the theft in Police Court and later pleaded guilty in Hustings Court to resisting the officer.

framing.detail: Under the head 'Shot by a Policeman' the Dispatch said the officer 'was forced' to shoot and described Wills as 'a noted thief' who 'has borne a desperate character'; later court notes called him 'the colored snatch-thief'.

conflicts.note: The Dispatch said Wills used several aliases; the Hustings Court report links the names Wills and Jackson.

versions.value: tried 'yesterday', i.e. December 3, per the Dec. 4 paper

conflicts.note: Minor; the Dec. 4 issue reports the trial as held the day before.
